newsitem.title: CANADA: Nortel Q1 earnings top analysts' expectations.
newsitem.headline: Nortel Q1 earnings top analysts' expectations.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd. beat analysts' estimates on Tuesday, reporting a 28 percent increase in first-quarter earnings.
Brampton, Ontario-based Nortel said earnings rose to $112 million, or 41 cents a share, in the first quarter from $83 million, or 32 cents a share, in the same period a year earlier.
Sales rose to $3.35 billion in the quarter from $2.6 billion.
Chief Executive Jean Monty said in a telephone interview that the telecommunications equipment company's revenues should grow by 15 to 20 percent in 1997.
"We still maintain that we can meet our targets and that the revenue growth will be in the minimum mid-teens. So it's probably going to be between the 15 and 20 percent range," Monty said.
He noted that Nortel fared well in comparison with U.S. rival Lucent Technologies Inc. in the quarter. Lucent was spun off last year from AT&T.
Lucent said last week that it earned $66 million, or 10 cents a share, in its second quarter ended March 31, after a year-earlier quarterly loss of $103 million or 16 cents a share.
Nortel's stock surged on the earnings. The shares hit a high of C$95.45 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Tuesday before pulling back to trade up C$3.20 at C$95.15
In New York, Nortel rose $2.375 to $68.125, off a session peak of $68.375.
"Nortel we view as a core investment holding, and these guys really posted a very strong first quarter," said Jim Parmalee, an industry analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Parmalee said he had expected first-quarter earnings per share of 37 cents. Consensus estimates were 38 cents.
